prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1223; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a rear-end collision at low speed and says the other vehicle struck the back of the insured car. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer, and the driver is confirmed as the person named on the policy.

Entry 2: The police report and two independent witnesses place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of the collision. The other driver also describes the accident the same way, and the scene photos match the account.

Entry 3: The repair estimate shows damage that is mostly in line with the described impact, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known. The impact was very light, yet the claimant reports a severe neck injury, which does not fit the crash.

Entry 4: The claimant later added a few small details about seating position and the moment of braking, but the core account has stayed the same. A neighbor has told us the car appeared to be damaged some weeks before the claimed event, and this needs follow-up.

Entry 5: No earlier injury to the neck or upper back is known from the medical records received so far. Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved.

Entry 6: File reviewed. The claim stays open pending follow-up on the neighbor's statement and a final medical review.
